parts.label: (a)
parts.text: From Source 1, identify how the number of people living in extreme poverty has changed.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: From Source 2, identify two problems caused by increased globalisation.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Which problem caused by increased globalisation do you think is the most significant? Explain
why.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Explain why globalisation is an important national issue.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
‘Globalisation has many benefits.’
What are the strengths and weaknesses of the argument supporting this claim?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
‘Globalisation helps us understand other cultures.’
How could you test this claim? You should consider the types of information, sources of
evidence and methods you might use.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify one prediction from Daan’s statement. Explain why it is a prediction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain why Gabriella’s statement may be seen as a vested interest.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Which argument is more convincing, Daan’s or Gabriella’s?
Your answer should consider both arguments and you should support your point of view with
their words.
You should also consider:
• the strength of their reasoning and evidence
• their use of language
• the different kinds of information used.

text: ‘We should increase employment by encouraging globalisation.’
Do you agree with this statement?
• give reasons and evidence to support your opinion
• use the material in the sources and/or any of your own ideas
